review_note: Every quote was checked word for word against the official document on the review date (scripts/commitments/verify_sources.py). Edit this file only with a new review.
statistics_source: Eurostat tran_sf_roadus (road deaths), as published in observations.json

commitments.title: Halve road deaths and serious injuries between 2020 and 2030
commitments.nature: Policy objective of the European Commission, part of the EU Road Safety Policy Framework 2021–2030. Not legally binding.

sources.title: EU Road Safety Policy Framework 2021–2030 – Next steps towards ‘Vision Zero’
sources.location: Section 3.2, p. 11
sources.quote: It also proposed new interim targets of reducing the number of road deaths by 50% between 2020 and 2030 as well as reducing the number of serious injuries by 50% in the same period, as recommended in the Valletta Declaration.

sources.title: Europe on the Move – Sustainable Mobility for Europe: safe, connected, and clean
sources.location: Section 2 (Safe mobility)
sources.quote: The EU will also pursue new interim targets to reduce the number of road deaths by 50 per cent between 2020 and 2030 as well as to reduce the number of serious injuries by 50 per cent in the same period (using the new common definition of serious injury agreed with all Member States).

monitoring_baselines.note: The European Commission's own progress charts measure this target against 2019: its 2025 road safety statistics show the 2030 target as 11 400 deaths, half of the 22 800 recorded in 2019. The overview page of this dashboard uses the same 2019 baseline.

source.title: Road safety statistics 2025 in more detail, Figure 1 “EU target: halving road deaths by 2030”
source.publisher: European Commission, DG Mobility and Transport

targets.not_measured_reason: No official EU-wide series of serious injuries (MAIS3+) exists to measure this. The Commission only estimates about 100,000 a year as five per road death, and national MAIS3+ figures are incomplete; police-reported figures use other definitions.

commitments.title: Valletta Declaration: Member States commit to halving road deaths by 2020 and to a 2030 serious-injury target
commitments.issuer: Council of the European Union (transport ministers of the Member States)
commitments.nature: Political commitment by the Member States, adopted as Council conclusions. Not legally binding.

sources.title: Council conclusions on road safety – endorsing the Valletta Declaration of March 2017
sources.location: Annex to the annex (Valletta Declaration), point 8(a)
sources.quote: Member States will undertake to: a) continue and reinforce measures necessary to halve the number of road deaths in the EU by 2020 from the 2010 baseline;

sources.title: Council conclusions on road safety – endorsing the Valletta Declaration of March 2017
sources.location: Annex to the annex (Valletta Declaration), point 8(i)
sources.quote: set a target of halving the number of serious injuries in the EU by 2030 from the 2020 baseline using this common definition and in the framework of an overall road safety strategy for this period;

targets.scope_note: Set for the EU as it was in 2010 (27 Member States including the United Kingdom, without Croatia). The figures shown are for the current EU-27, so they approximate the original scope.

targets.description: Set a target to halve serious injuries (MAIS3+) from 2020 to 2030
targets.not_measured_reason: No official EU-wide series of serious injuries (MAIS3+) exists to measure this. The Commission only estimates about 100,000 a year as five per road death, and national MAIS3+ figures are incomplete; police-reported figures use other definitions.

commitments.title: Move close to zero road deaths by 2050 (“Vision Zero”)
commitments.nature: Long-term goal of the European Commission. Not legally binding and not quantified as a number.

sources.title: White Paper: Roadmap to a Single European Transport Area – Towards a competitive and resource efficient transport system
sources.location: Section 2.5, goal 9
sources.quote: By 2050, move close to zero fatalities in road transport. In line with this goal, the EU aims at halving road casualties by 2020.

sources.title: Europe on the Move – Sustainable Mobility for Europe: safe, connected, and clean
sources.location: Section 2 (Safe mobility)
sources.quote: The EU's long-term goal will remain moving as close as possible to zero fatalities in road transport by 2050 ("Vision Zero"). The same should be achieved for serious injuries.

targets.description: Close to zero road deaths by 2050
targets.not_measured_reason: The goal is not expressed as a number, so no target value is calculated. The latest official figure is shown for reference.

commitments.title: Halve road deaths between 2010 and 2020
commitments.nature: Strategic target of the European Commission's Policy Orientations on Road Safety 2011–2020. Not legally binding.

sources.title: Towards a European road safety area: policy orientations on road safety 2011–2020
sources.location: Section 3.2
sources.quote: the Commission proposes to continue with the target of halving the overall number of road deaths in the European Union by 2020 starting from 2010.

targets.scope_note: Set for the EU as it was in 2010 (27 Member States including the United Kingdom, without Croatia). The figures shown are for the current EU-27, so they approximate the original scope.

commitments.title: Halve road deaths by 2010
commitments.scope: European Union (15 Member States at the time)
commitments.nature: Target of the third European Road Safety Action Programme. Not legally binding.

sources.title: European Road Safety Action Programme – Halving the number of road accident victims in the European Union by 2010: A shared responsibility
sources.location: Section 2.2 (Monitoring the target)
sources.quote: Reduce the number of road deaths by 50% by 2010.

targets.not_measured_reason: The document does not state a baseline year, and the target was set for the EU of 15 Member States, so it cannot be compared reliably with the current EU-27 figures.

commitments.title: Slovenia: at most 50 road deaths in 2030
commitments.issuer: National Assembly of the Republic of Slovenia (resolution of 28 November 2023)
commitments.nature: Resolution on the National Road Safety Programme 2023–2030 (ReNPVCP23–30), adopted by the National Assembly and published in the official gazette, Uradni list RS 124/2023. Not legally binding. Serious injuries are to be no more than 400 in 2030, measured with Slovenian police data, which this site does not cover.

sources.title: Resolucija o nacionalnem programu varnosti cestnega prometa za obdobje od 2023 do 2030 (ReNPVCP23–30)
sources.location: Section 3.5, “Cilji resolucije za obdobje od leta 2023 do leta 2030”
sources.quote: Z izvajanjem ukrepov, določenih v resoluciji, bo stremela k temu, da na slovenskih cestah do leta 2030 ne bo umrlo več kot 50 oseb in da se v prometnih nesrečah ne bo hudo telesno poškodovalo več kot 400 oseb. Za izhodiščno leto je uporabljeno leto 2019

translation.text: By implementing the measures set out in the resolution, [Slovenia] will strive to ensure that by 2030 no more than 50 people die on Slovenian roads and no more than 400 are seriously injured in road traffic crashes. 2019 is used as the baseline year

targets.description: At most 50 road deaths in 2030 (baseline year 2019)
targets.scope_note: The resolution states the target as a maximum of 50 road deaths, not as a percentage. Eurostat records 102 road deaths in Slovenia in 2019, the resolution's baseline year, so the target implies a change of −51.0 %.

commitments.title: Spain: halve road deaths between 2019 and 2030
commitments.issuer: Dirección General de Tráfico (DGT), Ministry of the Interior
commitments.nature: National road safety strategy of Spain (Estrategia de Seguridad Vial 2030). Not legally binding. It also sets a −50 % target for serious injuries, measured with police records (8,613 in 2019), which this site does not cover.

sources.title: Estrategia de Seguridad Vial 2030
sources.location: Resumen ejecutivo, “Los objetivos del decenio”, p. 20 of the PDF
sources.quote: En 2030, reducir el número de personas fallecidas en un 50% respecto al valor base de 2019 (1.755).

translation.text: By 2030, a 50% reduction in fatalities compared to 2019 (1,755).
translation.title: Road Safety Strategy 2030 – Summary (official English version)

targets.scope_note: The strategy's baseline (1,755 deaths in 2019) equals the Eurostat figure for Spain.

commitments.title: Poland: halve road deaths by 2030, to no more than 1,455
commitments.issuer: Krajowa Rada Bezpieczeństwa Ruchu Drogowego (National Road Safety Council)
commitments.nature: National road safety programme of Poland (Narodowy Program Bezpieczeństwa Ruchu Drogowego 2021–2030). Not legally binding. It also sets a −50 % target for seriously injured people (no more than 5,317), measured with national police records, which this site does not cover.

sources.title: Narodowy Program Bezpieczeństwa Ruchu Drogowego 2021–2030
sources.location: Streszczenie (summary), p. 24 of the PDF
sources.quote: głównym celem Narodowego Programu Bezpieczeństwa Ruchu Drogowego 2021-2030 będzie ograniczenie w ciągu dekady o 50% liczby ofiar śmiertelnych i ciężko rannych. Oznacza to, iż w roku 2030 na polskich drogach liczba ofiar śmiertelnych wypadków nie powinna przekroczyć wartości 1455, a liczba ofiar ciężko rannych nie powinna być większa niż 5317.

translation.text: the main goal of the National Road Safety Programme 2021-2030 will be to reduce the number of fatalities and seriously injured victims by 50% within a decade. This means that in 2030 on Polish roads the number of road accident fatalities should not exceed 1455, and the number of seriously injured victims should not exceed 5317.
translation.title: National Road Safety Programme 2021–2030 (official English version)

targets.scope_note: The programme states the target as “no more than 1455 in 2030” without naming a baseline year in that sentence. 1,455 is half of the 2,909 deaths in 2019, which the programme gives as its starting point and which equals the Eurostat figure, so 2019 is used as the baseline.

commitments.title: Germany: 40 % fewer road deaths by 2030
commitments.issuer: Federal Government of Germany (Federal Ministry of Transport)
commitments.nature: Road safety programme of the German Federal Government 2021–2030 (Verkehrssicherheitsprogramm der Bundesregierung 2021 bis 2030), agreed with the federal states. Not legally binding. Serious injuries are to fall “significantly”, without a number.

sources.title: Verkehrssicherheitsprogramm der Bundesregierung 2021 bis 2030
sources.publisher: Bundesministerium für Verkehr und digitale Infrastruktur
sources.location: Chapter I, “Mehr Verkehrssicherheit gemeinsam erreichen”, p. 7 of the PDF
sources.quote: Gemeinsam hat man sich darauf verständigt, die Zahl der Verkehrstoten in Deutschland bis 2030 um 40 % zu reduzieren und die Zahl der Schwerverletzten signifikant senken zu wollen.

translation.text: It was jointly agreed to reduce the number of road deaths in Germany by 40 % by 2030 and to aim for a significant reduction in the number of seriously injured people.

targets.not_measured_reason: The programme does not state a baseline year for the 40 % reduction, so no target value is calculated.

commitments.title: Austria: halve road deaths by 2030, from the 2017–2019 average
commitments.issuer: Austrian Federal Government (Federal Ministry for Climate Action, BMK; now BMIMI)
commitments.nature: Austrian Road Safety Strategy 2021–2030 (Österreichische Verkehrssicherheitsstrategie 2021–2030), published by the federal transport ministry in German and in its own English edition. Not legally binding. Serious injuries are also to fall by 50 % from the 2017–2019 average, measured with Austrian police data, which this site does not cover; no child is to be killed in road traffic by 2030.

sources.title: Austrian Road Safety Strategy 2021–2030
sources.publisher: Federal Ministry for Climate Action, Environment, Energy, Mobility, Innovation and Technology (BMK)
sources.location: Chapter 6.1, “Reduction targets”, p. 59 of the PDF
sources.quote: 50 % reduction in traffic fatalities by 2030 (basis: average 2017 – 2019)

sources.title: Verkehrssicherheit in Österreich – Jahresbericht 2024
sources.publisher: Federal Ministry for Innovation, Mobility and Infrastructure (BMIMI)
sources.location: p. 23 of the PDF; gives the baseline as 413 deaths and the target as 206
sources.quote: In der Verkehrssicherheitsstrategie 2021–2030 werden bei den numerischen Reduktionszielen die durchschnittlichen Werte der Jahre 2017–2019 als Ausgangsbasis herangezogen. Damit ergeben sich als Ausgangs- sowie Zielwerte: • Getötete: Ausgangswert 413, Zielwert 206

translation.title: Road Safety in Austria – Annual Report 2024 (English edition)
translation.text: The 2021–2030 road safety strategy uses the average values from 2017–2019 as a baseline for its numerical reduction targets. These baseline and target figures are as follows: • Fatalities: baseline figure 413, target figure 206

targets.description: Road deaths −50 % by 2030, from the 2017–2019 average
targets.scope_note: The 2017–2019 average of Eurostat's figures for Austria (413.0) equals the ministry's baseline of 413 road deaths; half of it is 206.5, which the ministry rounds to 206.

commitments.title: Croatia: halve road deaths by 2030, from 2019
commitments.issuer: Government of the Republic of Croatia (decision of 29 July 2021)
commitments.nature: National Road Safety Plan of the Republic of Croatia 2021–2030 (Nacionalni plan sigurnosti cestovnog prometa), adopted by Government decision and published in the official gazette, Narodne novine 86/2021. Not legally binding. The plan also aims to halve the number of serious crashes (crashes with deaths or serious injuries), which this site does not cover.

sources.title: Odluka o donošenju Nacionalnog plana sigurnosti cestovnog prometa Republike Hrvatske za razdoblje od 2021. do 2030.
sources.publisher: Narodne novine (official gazette of the Republic of Croatia)
sources.location: Preface (Predgovor) of the plan
sources.quote: Opći cilj Nacionalnog plana usmjeren je na ostvarenje 50% smanjenja broja osoba poginulih u prometnim nesrećama i broja teških prometnih nesreća u cestovnom prometu.

translation.text: The general objective of the National Plan is a 50 % reduction in the number of people killed in road traffic crashes and in the number of serious road traffic crashes.

sources.title: Odluka o donošenju Nacionalnog plana sigurnosti cestovnog prometa Republike Hrvatske za razdoblje od 2021. do 2030.
sources.publisher: Narodne novine (official gazette of the Republic of Croatia)
sources.location: Introduction to the analysis of critical factors; the preface gives 297 road deaths in 2019
sources.quote: S obzirom na dinamiku i metodologiju obrade podataka te provođenje istraživanja i izradu Nacionalnog plana u 2020., kao referentna godina korištena je 2019.

translation.text: Given the timing and method of data processing and the research and drafting of the National Plan in 2020, 2019 was used as the reference year.

targets.scope_note: The plan gives 297 road deaths in 2019, equal to Eurostat's figure for Croatia; half of it is 148.5.

commitments.title: Czechia: halve road deaths and serious injuries by 2030
commitments.issuer: Government of the Czech Republic (resolution no. 8 of 4 January 2021)
commitments.nature: Road Safety Strategy BESIP 2021–2030 (Strategie BESIP 2021–2030), approved by the Government and published by the Ministry of Transport. Not legally binding. The strategy counts deaths within 24 hours of a crash; Eurostat's figures use 30 days.

sources.title: Strategie BESIP 2021–2030
sources.location: Chapter 1, “Úvod”, p. 4 of the PDF
sources.quote: snížit počet usmrcených a těžce zraněných osob na pozemních komunikacích o polovinu (v roce 2030 o 50 % méně vůči výchozímu stavu). Pozn. Výchozí stav předpokladu Strategie je průměrem let 2017-2019.

translation.text: to halve the number of people killed and seriously injured on the roads (50 % fewer in 2030 than at the starting point). Note: the Strategy's starting point is the average of 2017–2019.

sources.title: Strategie BESIP 2021–2030
sources.location: Section 3.1, “Mezní hodnoty usmrcených a těžce zraněných osob”, p. 11 of the PDF
sources.quote: vinu, tzn. v roce 2030 o 50 % méně vůči roku 2020.

translation.text: [to] half, i.e. 50 % fewer in 2030 than in 2020.

targets.not_measured_reason: The strategy gives two different baselines: the average of 2017–2019 in its introduction and 2020 in section 3.1. No target value is calculated; the latest official figure is shown for reference.

commitments.title: Second Decade of Action for Road Safety: at least 50 % fewer road deaths and injuries from 2021 to 2030
commitments.nature: UN General Assembly resolution. Not legally binding; it invites action by UN Member States, including all EU Member States.

sources.title: Improving global road safety (resolution A/RES/74/299)
sources.location: Operative paragraph 3
sources.quote: Proclaims the period 2021–2030 as the Second Decade of Action for Road Safety, with a goal of reducing road traffic deaths and injuries by at least 50 per cent from 2021 to 2030

targets.description: Road traffic deaths and injuries at least −50 % from 2021 to 2030 (global goal)
targets.not_measured_reason: A global goal; this dashboard covers the EU only.

commitments.title: Stockholm Declaration: at least 50 % fewer road deaths from 2020 to 2030
commitments.issuer: Third Global Ministerial Conference on Road Safety
commitments.nature: Declaration of ministers and heads of delegation, later endorsed by the UN General Assembly (A/RES/74/299). Not legally binding.

sources.title: Stockholm Declaration – Third Global Ministerial Conference on Road Safety: Achieving Global Goals 2030
sources.publisher: Third Global Ministerial Conference on Road Safety (hosted by the Government of Sweden)
sources.location: Point 3 ("we hereby resolve to")
sources.quote: Call upon Member States to contribute to reducing road traffic deaths by at least 50% from 2020 to 2030

targets.description: Road traffic deaths at least −50 % from 2020 to 2030 (global)
targets.not_measured_reason: A global goal; this dashboard covers the EU only.

commitments.title: Sweden: halve road deaths by 2030, from the 2017–2019 average
commitments.nature: Interim target (etappmål) of Sweden's transport policy towards Vision Zero, decided by the Government on 13 February 2020 and quantified by the Swedish Transport Administration (Trafikverket). Not legally binding. Serious injuries are to fall by at least 25 %, measured with Swedish hospital-based data, which this site does not cover.

sources.title: Nya mål för trafiksäkerhet väg 2020–2030 (PM)
sources.location: p. 1, “Nytt transportpolitiskt etappmål för trafiksäkerhet”; footnote 1 gives the road baseline as 266 deaths a year and the 2030 target as at most 133
sources.quote: Antalet omkomna till följd av trafikolyckor inom vägtrafiken, sjöfarten respektive luftfarten ska halveras till år 2030. Antalet omkomna inom bantrafiken ska halveras till år 2030. Antalet allvarligt skadade inom respektive trafikslag ska till år 2030 minska med minst 25 procent. Utgångsvärdet för etappmålet utgörs av ett medelvärde av utfallet för år 2017, 2018 och 2019.

translation.text: The number of people killed as a result of traffic accidents in road traffic, shipping and aviation respectively shall be halved by 2030. The number killed in rail traffic shall be halved by 2030. The number of seriously injured in each mode of transport shall fall by at least 25 per cent by 2030. The baseline for the interim target is the average of the outcomes for 2017, 2018 and 2019.

targets.description: Road deaths −50 % by 2030, from the 2017–2019 average
targets.scope_note: The target also covers shipping and aviation; only road deaths are measured here. The 2017–2019 average of Eurostat's figures for Sweden (266.0) equals Trafikverket's baseline of 266 road deaths a year, so the target is at most 133 in 2030.

commitments.title: Netherlands: towards zero road casualties
commitments.issuer: Dutch central government, provinces, municipalities and regions
commitments.nature: Strategic road safety plan of the Dutch governments (Strategisch Plan Verkeersveiligheid 2030), led by the Ministry of Infrastructure and Water Management. Not legally binding. It sets no national number of deaths for 2030; results for 2030 are set per theme and by each road authority.

sources.title: Veilig van deur tot deur: Het Strategisch Plan Verkeersveiligheid 2030
sources.location: Chapter 2, p. 13 of the PDF; Figure 3 on the same page gives this as the overarching ambition for 2050 (“Op weg naar nul slachtoffers”)
sources.quote: Het streven is nul verkeersslachtoffers. Overheden leveren samen met maatschappelijke partners maximale inspanning om zoveel mogelijk risico’s weg te nemen door het verbeteren van wegen en voertuigen én het beïnvloeden van menselijk gedrag.

translation.text: The aim is zero road casualties. Governments, together with partners in society, make every effort to remove as many risks as possible by improving roads and vehicles and by influencing human behaviour.

targets.not_measured_reason: The aim is not expressed as a number, so no target value is calculated. The latest official figure is shown for reference.
